chapter: Europe tours, Birdland memories and closing
title: Arnett Cobb and the Mobb at the Zanzibar; Charlie Barnet breaks his horn
summary: At the Zanzibar a Daily News critic called Cobb's six-piece group a mob, giving the name the Mobb, while Charlie Barnet bent his soprano sax over his leg in a domestic row.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: All right, Arnett, now we're nearly up to date. What are those other things you've got for me?

Well, I wanted to let you know when I was working at the Zanzibar in New York at 49th and Broadway -- they had a guy from the Daily News that was a critic. I can't think of Bob's last name. Maybe you would know who he was, the musical critic for the Daily News.

No, this was in the '50s, early '50s. But anyhow, I had six pieces with Bootie, me and Dave Page. Rhythm section was Joe Harris. Bass player -- what was his name? Walter Buchanan. And the piano player was George Phil Joey Rhodes. Of course, here I am again, six pieces. But he said it sounded like a mob, six pieces. And we're working opposite of Barnet, Charlie Barnet. And Charlie would come on and play,

and then we'd come on and play, and he said, you sound like a mob. So he gave me the name Arnett Cobb and the Mobb -- (Laughter) -- spelled with two Bs, M-o-b-b. And he was the one that was instrumental in getting me in Birdland.

But on this particular date Charlie Barnet went up there to talk to California, and he had some -- what them long necked things, birds, long neck -- ostriches? He had some and somebody (inaudible) he talked to his old lady, and they were getting along bad. He was having domestic trouble, and he come down on the bandstand on his next (inaudible) set and took his soprano saxophone and took it across his leg and bent it and told everybody, "I'm through with the music business" and threw it on the floor and walked back out.
I said I don't believe this. He's stone millionaire. He can buy another tomorrow. But I ain't going be that crazy to break mine over my leg. Nothing --
I'm just going back into business from my operation, you know, and things.
Well, I hope to fit that in here.
But it was the latter part, but he was instrumental -- he said, "You should be down in Birdland." So
